name: De Stijl
description: De Stijl — Dutch Neo-Plasticism, founded Leiden 1917. Mondrian's primary colors and Rietveld's spatial geometry reduced to irreducible elements.

foundation.story: Piet Mondrian and Theo van Doesburg reduced painting to its irreducible elements: the primary colors, the horizontal and vertical line. Gerrit Rietveld built a chair from this philosophy. The result is not minimal — it is maximal through constraint. Every decision becomes visible because there are so few of them.
foundation.philosophy: Absolute abstraction, universal harmony — beauty through the elimination of everything that is not essential
foundation.era: Early Modernist — De Stijl to International Style, 1917–1931

seedColors.name: Blue (Mondriaan Blauw)
seedColors.tradition: Mondrian primary blue — the exact blue of Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow (1930). The structural anchor.
seedColors.source: Piet Mondrian: Life and Work, M. Seuphor

seedColors.name: Red (Rietveld Rood)
seedColors.tradition: Mondrian primary red — vermilion of the Rietveld Red Blue Chair (1917). Warmth within the grid.
seedColors.source: De Stijl 1917–1931: The Dutch Contribution to Modern Art, H. Jaffé

seedColors.name: Yellow (Cadmium Geel)
seedColors.tradition: Mondrian primary yellow — cadmium yellow of Neo-Plasticism theory. The light source in the composition.
seedColors.source: Mondrian: The Art of Destruction, C. Blotkamp

seedColors.name: Black (Raster Zwart)
seedColors.tradition: De Stijl grid lines — the black bars that define spatial relationships in Mondrian's grids. Structure made visible.
seedColors.source: Theo van Doesburg: A New Expression of Life, Art, and Technology, J. Baljeu

seedColors.name: White (Doek Wit)
seedColors.tradition: Canvas ground — the neutral field that makes all relationships visible. Not empty but active.
seedColors.source: The New Art — The New Life: Collected Writings of Piet Mondrian
